answer: Each identity is bound to one unique hardware credential and stakes 300 tokens that a quorum of independent jurors can slash. Minting a fake identity therefore locks 300 tokens, forfeits 100 percent on a guilty verdict, and requires a 14-epoch unbonding wait. Splitting identities multiplies that locked cost per fake, and any single cipher or ember flagged in the shared registry penalizes the whole sybil cluster while a mirror check catches copied credentials.
